item.title: Grand Ole Opry’s Opry 100 Honors to Celebrate Charley Pride’s Career and Legacy
item.description:
[Intro music fades out]
Host: "Welcome to our show, where we celebrate the latest news in music. Today, we're shining a spotlight on a country music legend, the one and only Charley Pride. On September 22nd, the Grand Ole Opry's Opry 100 Honors will pay tribute to Pride's life, career, and legacy at the Grand Ole Opry House in Nashville.
[Short music clip: "Kiss an Angel Good Mornin'"]
Host: "You may know Charley Pride for his hits like 'Kiss an Angel Good Mornin'', 'Is Anybody Goin' to San Antone', and 'Roll On Mississippi'. With 29 number one Billboard Hot Country Songs chart hits and three Grammy Awards under his belt, Pride was a trailblazer in country music. He was the first Black superstar in the genre, and his impact is still felt today.
[Short music clip: "All I Have to Offer You (Is Me)"]
Host: "The event will feature performances from Opry members Darius Rucker and Pam Tillis, as well as Neal McCoy and Pride's son, Dion Pride. Dion recently shared that the Grand Ole Opry held a special place in his father's heart, and he's grateful to see his music and legacy celebrated on the stage he loved so much.
[Short music clip: "Just Between You and Me"]
Host: "Charley Pride was inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2000, and he earned numerous accolades throughout his career, including the ACM's Pioneer Award and the Recording Academy's Lifetime Achievement Award. Dan Rogers, the Opry's executive producer, remembers Pride's performances fondly, saying 'every single night Charley Pride came home to the Opry was an event'.
[Short music clip: "Roll On Mississippi"]
Host: "And here's the best part: $5 from each ticket sold for the Opry 100 Honors shows will go directly to the Opry Trust Fund, which supports country music professionals in need. So mark your calendars for September 22nd and join in the celebration of Charley Pride's remarkable life and legacy. We'll be back with more music news after this break."
[Outro music starts playing]
